diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\mathcal{R}_z \gets$ compute cyclotomic factorization of the ratio via Eq.~\eqref{eq:ratio_Rz}

issues.failure_explanation: From the summand in eq:racah_6j, T_{z+1}/T_z = -[z+2]_q \prod_y [b_y - z]_q / \prod_i [z+1-a_i]_q: the factors [z+1-a_i] belong in the denominator (they come from 1/[z+1-a_i]!) and the factors from [b_y - z]!/[b_y-z-1]! = [b_y - z] belong in the numerator. The stated ratio puts [z+1-a_i] in the numerator and [b_y-(z+1)] in the denominator. Moreover, at z = z_max - 1 one has b_y - (z+1) = 0 for the minimizing y, so the stated denominator contains [0]_q = 0 and the ratio is undefined. The DCR definition and Algorithm 1 construct the ratio sequence 'via Eq. ratio_Rz', so as written the compiled object does not encode the 6j series.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace eq:ratio_Rz by R_z = -[z+2]_q \prod_{y=1}^3 [b_y - z]_q / \prod_{i=1}^4 [z+1-a_i]_q (and use it in Algorithm 1 and the DCR definition).
issues.overall_effect: The compiled sequence {R_z} (Definition of the DCR, Algorithm 1) and the identity S(q)=\Pi_q(S_DCR) for the 6j-symbol are incorrect if the printed formula is used; the correction requires rederiving the recurrence, not a single visible substitution.
issues.title: Update ratio R_z for the 6j-symbol is inverted and shifted; literal formula divides by [0]_q at the last step
issues.why_classification: A short local rederivation of the ratio fixes the construction; all results, complexity claims and the framework survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The intrinsic sensitivity of the problem is governed by the condition number (Eq.~\eqref{eq:condition_num}), which is independent of representation.
and the numerical error is driven primarily by the intrinsic condition number $\kappa$.

issues.failure_explanation: The paragraph asserts that the cancellations responsible for the condition number kappa are performed exactly at the algebraic level and no longer realized numerically. kappa = sum|T_z|/|S| measures cancellation between different alternating summands, which the exponent-vector arithmetic (acting within a single summand) cannot remove; the paper's own error bound eq:forwd_error retains the intrinsic term kappa Z epsilon, states kappa is representation-independent, and Table tab:phase_flip shows DCR failing at j=110 as kappa grows. What the DCR reduces is only the representation factor gamma_rep.

failure_location.quote: the large intermediate cancellations to resolve the condition number $\kappa$ in Section~\ref{subsec:cancellation} are no longer realized numerically, but are instead resolved exactly at the algebraic level.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rephrase the claim to say that the DCR removes the representation-induced amplification gamma_rep while the intrinsic kappa-cancellation of the alternating sum remains and is only mitigated, consistent with eq:forwd_error.
issues.overall_effect: The stated mechanism for numerical stability is overstated; the actual guarantee is a reduction of gamma_rep (roughly a factor ~9 in Table tab:dynamic_range), not elimination of the kappa-driven precision loss.
issues.title: Prose claims the alternating-sum cancellation (condition number kappa) is resolved algebraically by the DCR, contradicting the paper's own error analysis
issues.why_classification: A local rewording aligned with the paper's own analysis suffices; no formal result changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For symbolic evaluation, one may take $\mathbb{T} = \Q(\zeta_{2h})$, the cyclotomic number field generated by a primitive root $\zeta_{2h}$.
The entire square root is resolved at the exponent level, without field extension and without any polynomial computation.
where $\sigma \in \{-1,1\}$, $P \in \Z$, and $\mathbf{e}$ is a cyclotomic exponent vector.

issues.failure_explanation: The odd-exponent part M_rad is a nontrivial monomial in general (e.g. Delta_{abc} contains sqrt of ratios of quantum integers), and its projected value need not be a square in T. For T = Q(zeta_{2h}) the element sqrt(Pi(M_rad)) generally lies outside T (e.g. sqrt([2]_q) = 2^{1/4} for h=4 is not in Q(zeta_8)), so the Ensure 'S in T' and the exact-field regime as stated fail; the square root is not 'resolved without field extension' at evaluation. For complex T the monomial Pi(M_rad) (including a q^P factor with possibly odd P and complex Phi_d(q^2)) is not positive real, so sqrt is branch-dependent and the algorithm's output is determined only up to sign, whereas the 6j-symbol is defined with the positive real triangle coefficients.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the exact-field guarantee to returning the pair (Pi(M_rad), Pi(M_root) S_sum) or S^2, or work in the quadratic extension T(sqrt(Pi(M_rad))); for numeric fields specify the branch (e.g. take the positive root of Pi(M_root)^2 Pi(M_rad), which is real positive for admissible spins on the unit circle) and adjust the prose accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm 2's output contract fails for exact cyclotomic fields and is sign-ambiguous for complex evaluation; the identity S(q)=Pi_q(S_DCR) is only established up to a branch choice for the radical prefactor; the claim that square roots require no field extension holds only at compile time.
issues.title: Final square-root step of the projection is not in the target field and has an unspecified branch
issues.why_classification: A contained modification of the projection step and a limited weakening of the exact-field output guarantee resolve it; the framework survives but the advertised 'exact evaluation in Q(zeta_{2h}) without field extension' must be qualified.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This produces a dense table in $\mathcal{O}(D \log D)$ time, eliminating repeated factorization or symbolic expansion.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition (given without proof) charges D_max C_T for the precomputation of the cyclotomic table, but Section 4 states the Möbius-inversion table costs O(D log D) field operations (sum over n of tau(n)). In addition, projecting M_base requires ~D_max exponentiations with exponents floor(n/d) up to D_max, each costing O(log D_max) multiplications, again exceeding the stated D_max C_T term.

failure_location.quote: \mathcal{O}\!\left( D_{\max} \cdot C_{\mathbb{T}} + Z \cdot K \cdot S_{\max} \cdot C_{\mathbb{T}} \right)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the bound as O(D_max log D_max C_T + Z K S_max C_T) (or justify an O(D_max) table construction) and supply the omitted proof.
issues.overall_effect: The stated evaluation bound is understated by logarithmic factors; the qualitative 'near-linear' conclusion survives.
issues.title: Evaluation complexity omits logarithmic factors the paper itself states elsewhere
issues.why_classification: Only a log factor in an unproven complexity statement; a local correction preserves all advertised scaling claims.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $|V|$ is the number of vertices, $\mathcal{A}$ is a global normalization constant, and $\tau$ indexes the constituent tetrahedra.
\Delta_{j_1 j_2 j_3} \, \Delta_{j_1 j_5 j_6}\, \Delta_{j_2 j_4 j_6} \,\Delta_{j_3 j_4 j_5} \times

issues.failure_explanation: The Turaev–Viro partition function includes a product over edges of quantum-dimension weights (e.g. (-1)^{2j_e}[2j_e+1]_q) in addition to the tetrahedral 6j-symbols; with the Racah-normalized symbol of eq:racah_6j these weights cannot be absorbed into the 6j factors or into a global constant A^{-|V|}. As displayed, the expression is not the Turaev–Viro invariant.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the product of edge weights prod_e w_{j_e} into eq:TV.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed formula used to motivate the state-sum application is incorrect; the amortization argument itself is unaffected since edge weights are quantum integers also representable in the DCR.
issues.title: Turaev–Viro state sum written without edge (quantum-dimension) weights
issues.why_classification: A local correction of an illustrative formula with no dependents.
